To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the installation of a biogas-fed solid oxide fuel cell cogeneration system in a wastewater treatment plant can reduce the environmental impacts of the plant, particularly the global warming potential and the primary energy demand.
a biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel cell (SOFC) cogeneration system can be an environmentally sound alternative for biogas utilization at the scale of a wastewater treatment plant.

the use of biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) for the cogeneration of electricity and heat in a wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) reduces the environmental burden associated with the plant operation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of sustainable solutions that can help in the transition towards the circular bio-economy.
the assessment of the environmental performance of an industrial-scale biogas-fed solid oxide fuel cell plant integrated in a wastewater treatment plant.
the environmental impact assessment of an integrated SOFC-WWT system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the installation of a SOFC cogeneration system in a WWTP can be considered as a sustainable and economically feasible option for the valorization of biogas.
the integration of an efficient biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFCs) cogeneration system in the WWTP is a promising solution to improve the environmental sustainability of the WWTP.

, in the specific case investigated, biogas-fed solid oxide fuel cells are a promising solution for wastewater treatment plants, as they can reduce the overall environmental impacts and, in the long run, can even be self-sustained.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel Cells for electricity and heat cogeneration can be an environmentally sound solution for wastewater treatment plants.

a biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel Cells (SOFC) cogeneration module can be considered as an environmentally-friendly solution for the exploitation of sewage biogas, especially in the presence of a high thermal demand in the WWTP, as in our case study.

the use of a biogas-fed Solid Oxide Fuel Cells system for the cogeneration of heat and electrical energy in a WWTP is an environmental friendly solution, which can be further improved if a thermal energy conservation system is integrated in the WWTP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when properly designed, SOFC cogeneration can be a viable alternative to conventional biogas exploitation technologies in the framework of WWTPs.

the use of SOFC-based cogenerations systems for biogas valorisation is a promising solution to improve the environmental sustainability of WWTPs, particularly when coupled with energy saving strategies.

, in order to be sustainable in the long run, biogas-based SOFC cogeneration systems should be integrated in the design phase with the wastewater treatment plant, in order to exploit the potential synergies between the two systems and to minimize the environmental impact associated with their operation.
